headline: Directory claims India's active Rafale fleet fell, sparking military pushback
summary: FlightGlobal’s 2027 World Air Forces directory lists 32 of India’s 36 Rafale jets as active, down from 35 in November 2025. Retired Air Marshal Narmdeshwar Tiwari dismissed the Cirium data as patently false on Thursday, saying listed jets flew in exercises, while officials questioned the unverified tally.
why_it_matters: Public fleet counts face intense scrutiny after the May conflict because India acknowledged aircraft losses without disclosing numbers, turning aviation tallies into contested claims.
source_search: Directory claims India's active Rafale fleet fell, sparking military pushback Scroll.in

headline: Anthropic’s seven founders cash out $1.95 billion in record IPO
summary: Anthropic went public on Thursday at $83 per share, raising $104.8 billion while its seven founders cashed out $1.95 billion. Nvidia, Google, and major chipmakers bought $26 billion in non-voting shares, leaving Amazon and Google with a 28 percent stake and giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion in working capital.
why_it_matters: Despite the record haul, Anthropic faces $70.7 billion in compute commitments over 12 months and $451.6 billion through 2030, proving frontier AI’s immense capital demands.
source_search: Anthropic’s seven founders cash out $1.95 billion in record IPO TechCrunch

headline: Supreme Court dismisses Tamil Nadu plea over Cauvery water shortfall
summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed Tamil Nadu's plea seeking 11.719 TMC of Cauvery water from Karnataka for the 2026-27 irrigation year. A bench led by Justice Vikram Nath rejected the claim after Karnataka argued Tamil Nadu received excess allocations, reinforcing the Cauvery Water Management Authority's regulatory role.
why_it_matters: Backing the expert water-sharing authority discourages states from repeatedly litigating distress-year shortfalls in court while leaving downstream farmers dependent on statutory reservoir releases.
source_search: Supreme Court dismisses Tamil Nadu plea over Cauvery water shortfall The Hindu

headline: Indian rupee strengthens past 93 per dollar on foreign inflows
summary: The Indian rupee jumped 50 paise to 92.82 against the US dollar on Friday, crossing the 93 mark for the first time since April 10. Foreign portfolio investors have injected over ₹84,000 crore into Indian equities over two weeks, lifting the Sensex 723 points and Nifty 218 points.
why_it_matters: Capital rotating out of US, Taiwanese, and South Korean AI rallies into Indian equities strengthens the currency even as Brent crude trades above $92.
source_search: Indian rupee strengthens past 93 per dollar on foreign inflows Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Maharashtra clarifies Dadar metro station, not rail hub, becomes Chaityabhoomi
summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis clarified on Thursday that Mumbai’s Dadar metro station, rather than its railway station, will be renamed Chaityabhoomi after the government deleted an earlier statement. Ahead of BR Ambedkar’s December 6 death anniversary, lawmakers will formalise the change during the Winter Session starting December 7.
why_it_matters: With 15 lakh visitors expected at Chaityabhoomi on December 6, the renaming clarification and protest ban signal Maharashtra’s focus on managing crowds and expediting the Ambedkar memorial.
source_search: Maharashtra clarifies Dadar metro station, not rail hub, becomes Chaityabhoomi Scroll.in

headline: Russian missiles hit three Kyiv bridges in massive retaliatory barrage
summary: Russia launched nearly 100 missiles and 400 drones overnight across nine Ukrainian regions, hitting three Kyiv bridges and killing six people. Strikes at a Lviv railway station killed two, while a projectile reportedly landed inside Poland. Authorities closed the Dnipro crossings as Polish jets scrambled near the border.
why_it_matters: Severing Kyiv's river crossings disrupts urban transport and supply lines while any spillover into Polish territory risks drawing NATO directly into an escalating retaliatory cycle.
source_search: Russian missiles hit three Kyiv bridges in massive retaliatory barrage BBC

headline: Supreme Court rejects PIL seeking police database of sexual offence complainants
summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a public interest plea seeking district police databases of people filing repeated sexual offence complaints. A bench including Chief Justice Surya Kant held that everyone has a right to complain and warned such registries would endanger victims' statutory privacy protections.
why_it_matters: Affirming that existing magistrate statements and forensic checks handle false allegations prevents police profiling that could deter sexual assault survivors from reporting crimes.
source_search: Supreme Court rejects PIL seeking police database of sexual offence complainants The Hindu

headline: Apple builds in-house Mac AI agent while tightening third-party access
summary: A recent Apple job listing reveals the company is developing an in-house AI agent capable of browsing, coding, and operating apps across Macs. Simultaneously, Bloomberg reports that Apple’s upcoming macOS 27.3 will introduce warnings discouraging users from granting full system control to competing third-party AI agents.
why_it_matters: Restricting rival computer-use agents while building a native assistant lets Apple tighten macOS security controls and retain users within its emerging AI ecosystem.
source_search: Apple builds in-house Mac AI agent while tightening third-party access TechCrunch

headline: Urban Company raises ₹2,500 crore in oversubscribed institutional share sale
summary: Home services platform Urban Company raised ₹2,500 crore on Friday through a qualified institutional placement that drew over ₹15,000 crore in bids. Priced at ₹156 per share, the issue saw strong participation from domestic mutual funds, insurers, and global investors to fund its InstaHelp ecosystem, technology, and acquisitions.
why_it_matters: Demand exceeding six times the offer, including 13 new shareholders, gives Urban Company capital to expand InstaHelp’s supply ecosystem and fund potential acquisitions.
source_search: Urban Company raises ₹2,500 crore in oversubscribed institutional share sale Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Telangana suspends licences of Karachi Bakery units, meat outlets over hygiene
summary: Telangana's food safety authority suspended FSSAI licences for six Hyderabad establishments on Thursday, including two Karachi Bakery units and four meat outlets. Inspectors seized 1,672 kg of food worth ₹6.59 lakh after finding rat droppings, expired prawns and chemicals beside food, shutting five unlicensed shops too.
why_it_matters: Targeting marquee regional brands alongside unlicenced processors signals tighter municipal enforcement of commercial hygiene standards in India's urban food supply chains.
source_search: Telangana suspends licences of Karachi Bakery units, meat outlets over hygiene The Hindu

headline: Trump, Putin and Xi issue joint peace declaration at Shenzhen summit
summary: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping issued a joint peace declaration on Thursday after 90-minute trilateral talks in Shenzhen during the APEC summit. They affirmed nuclear war cannot be fought, pledged higher petroleum supply, and opposed International Criminal Court overreach on officials' immunity while backing UN reform.
why_it_matters: Unprecedented three-way alignment on energy supply and restricting international court powers signals shifting great-power diplomacy, even as deep divisions persist over the Ukraine war.
source_search: Trump, Putin and Xi issue joint peace declaration at Shenzhen summit BBC

headline: SpaceX designs mini rooftop cell towers to fix indoor dead zones
summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk announced at the DealBook Summit that the company has finished designing miniature rooftop cell towers to eliminate indoor signal dead zones, with production targeted for 2027. Combined with SpaceX’s upcoming Direct-to-Cell V2 satellite constellation and acquired spectrum, the hardware aims to deliver ubiquitous coverage.
why_it_matters: Pairing $25 billion in wireless spectrum with terrestrial micro-towers addresses satellite internet’s biggest physical limitation, positioning SpaceX to compete harder with legacy telecoms.
source_search: SpaceX designs mini rooftop cell towers to fix indoor dead zones TechCrunch

headline: US panel accuses India of targeting Muslims in 130-million voter deletion
summary: The US Commission on International Religious Freedom accused India on Thursday of targeting Muslims during a voter roll revision that deleted 130 million names. Commissioners urged Washington to designate India a country of particular concern. India's Election Commission maintains the drive only removed duplicate, deceased and ineligible entries.
why_it_matters: Linking unprecedented electoral roll deletions to citizenship checks and deportations fuels domestic protests and adds diplomatic friction, even though USCIRF recommendations are non-binding.
source_search: US panel accuses India of targeting Muslims in 130-million voter deletion The Hindu

headline: Grain feedstocks power India to 20 percent ethanol blending milestone
summary: India reached an average ethanol blending level of 19.99 percent in the 2025-26 supply year, blending 1,134.36 crore litres through October 31. According to the All India Distillers’ Association, grain-based feedstocks supplied 73.52 percent of total ethanol, led by maize at 489.71 crore litres and surplus FCI rice.
why_it_matters: Relying predominantly on maize and surplus rice reduces India’s dependence on sugarcane for biofuel output while diversifying income avenues for agricultural producers.
source_search: Grain feedstocks power India to 20 percent ethanol blending milestone Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Jorrybell Agoto, star of Philippines Oscar contender Filipinana, dies at 32
summary: Actress Jorrybell Agoto, lead star of the Philippines’ international Oscar submission Filipinana, died on November 17 at age 32 after battling lymphoma. Production company Epicmedia announced her death on November 19 as the Sundance awardee opens in UK and Irish cinemas during its Academy shortlist campaign.
why_it_matters: Agoto’s death cuts short an indie career spanning Berlinale Talents and Gawad Urian recognition just as Filipinana places the Philippines’ cinema in international Academy contention.
source_search: Jorrybell Agoto, star of Philippines Oscar contender Filipinana, dies at 32 Variety

headline: Daily pill shrinks or halts advanced pancreatic tumours in early trial
summary: A daily KRAS inhibitor pill called daraxonrasib halted tumour growth in 90 percent of 61 advanced pancreatic cancer patients when paired with chemotherapy. Over 60 percent saw tumours shrink and one in 12 showed undetectable scans, nearly doubling disease control duration without proving a permanent cure.
why_it_matters: Targeting RAS mutations in a cancer with the lowest UK survival rate could extend patients' lives and eventually treat lung and ovarian tumours carrying similar genetic drivers.
source_search: Daily pill shrinks or halts advanced pancreatic tumours in early trial BBC

headline: Gujarat bans caste words and symbols on all private vehicles
summary: The Gujarat government on Friday announced a ban on caste-identifying words, symbols and signs on private vehicles, covering two-wheelers, cars, buses and trucks. Amending the 1989 Motor Vehicles Rules, the transport department barred caste signage unless specifically exempted after its June draft drew zero public objections.
why_it_matters: Bringing caste decals under formal motor-vehicle regulations gives traffic authorities enforceable grounds to curb public caste displays on state highways and city roads.
source_search: Gujarat bans caste words and symbols on all private vehicles Hindustan Times

headline: UN court finds Myanmar guilty of Rohingya genocide, orders safe return
summary: The International Court of Justice ruled on Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during its 2017 military crackdown, marking the court's first state genocide conviction. Judges ordered Myanmar to enable safe returns, prosecute perpetrators and pay reparations, though enforcement depends on the UN Security Council.
why_it_matters: The binding verdict gives displaced refugees in Cox's Bazar formal legal recognition and reparations backing, even if Myanmar's military leadership can ignore compliance orders.
source_search: UN court finds Myanmar guilty of Rohingya genocide, orders safe return The Hindu

headline: Meta’s pocket-sized Muse Charm AI wearable may retail for $300
summary: Meta plans to charge $300 for Muse Charm, its upcoming keychain-sized AI hardware device teased at Connect earlier this year, The Information reports. Designed to be carried in a pocket or worn around the neck, the wearable brings Meta’s Muse agentic assistant and interactive avatars into physical form.
why_it_matters: At $300, Meta faces steep consumer adoption hurdles after earlier AI wearables stumbled and rivals like Amazon’s Bee Frontier undercut it at $75.
source_search: Meta’s pocket-sized Muse Charm AI wearable may retail for $300 TechCrunch

headline: White House fires cyber chief Sean Cairncross after major network outages
summary: The White House fired National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross on Thursday following major outages across US travel, e-commerce and a top-secret government network. President Donald Trump backed the dismissal over Cairncross's credentials, naming Defense Department information chief Kirsten Davies as acting director amid growing AI threats.
why_it_matters: Replacing a political appointee with a Senate-confirmed defense official signals urgent pressure to secure critical US infrastructure and classified networks against escalating digital vulnerabilities.
source_search: White House fires cyber chief Sean Cairncross after major network outages The Hindu

headline: India’s October fertiliser sales fall 9 percent as winter sowing lags
summary: Overall Indian fertiliser sales dropped 9 percent year-on-year in October to 47.69 lakh tonnes as high complex fertiliser prices pushed complex sales down 44 percent. However, DAP sales rose 7 percent to 15.3 lakh tonnes, supporting optimism for Rabi sowing after overall acreage fell 11 percent through November 13.
why_it_matters: With wheat, mustard, and gram acreages trailing last year’s pace, timely fertiliser availability remains critical for hitting the government’s 177.72-million-tonne foodgrain target.
source_search: India’s October fertiliser sales fall 9 percent as winter sowing lags Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Asian Cup postponed to December 2027 amid attacks on host Saudi Arabia
summary: The Asian Football Confederation postponed its 24-team Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia from January 2027 to December 23, citing logistical and travel disruptions. Deadly Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure forced the shift, following regional disruptions to Formula One, tennis finals and the 2027 Dakar Rally.
why_it_matters: Resumed conflict with Houthi forces is now disrupting Saudi Arabia's heavy sports investments, forcing international federations to prioritise player safety over major tournament schedules.
source_search: Asian Cup postponed to December 2027 amid attacks on host Saudi Arabia DW

headline: Oscar winners Joachim Trier and Eskil Vogt win Göteborg honorary award
summary: Norwegian filmmakers Joachim Trier and Eskil Vogt, creators of 2026 Oscar winner Sentimental Value, will receive the Nordic Honorary Dragon Award at Sweden’s 50th Göteborg Film Festival. The duo will accept the festival’s top honour on January 29, alongside a retrospective celebrating 20 years of collaboration since Reprise.
why_it_matters: Honouring Trier and Vogt at its milestone 50th edition positions Göteborg to showcase Nordic cinema’s global Oscar momentum alongside past laureates like Thomas Vinterberg and Ruben Östlund.
source_search: Oscar winners Joachim Trier and Eskil Vogt win Göteborg honorary award Variety

headline: Tapati Guha Thakurta wins 2026 Oxford Bookstore Art Book Prize
summary: Art historian Tapati Guha Thakurta won the 2026 Oxford Bookstore Art Book Prize for editing From the Depth of the Mould, a centenary tribute to sculptor Meera Mukherjee. Published by Jadavpur University Press and Galerie 88, the Rs 1 lakh winner chronicles her work with metal crafting communities.
why_it_matters: Honouring archival scholarship alongside Bloomsbury and DAG special mentions strengthens academic and independent publishing dedicated to modern Indian art and traditional craft heritage.
source_search: Tapati Guha Thakurta wins 2026 Oxford Bookstore Art Book Prize Scroll.in

headline: Health trust says suspending Enniskillen emergency surgery improved patient outcomes
summary: Western Health Trust chief Karen Hargan told Stormont’s Health Committee that suspending emergency general surgery at Enniskillen’s South West Acute Hospital in 2022 improved patient mortality and complication rates. Despite legal action from local campaigners citing ambulance travel risks, officials plan a 2027 consultation on permanently ending the service.
why_it_matters: Centralising emergency surgery boosts clinical safety for transferred patients but leaves Fermanagh residents feeling abandoned while straining Altnagelvin’s overcrowded unit ahead of a proposed £73m overhaul.
source_search: Health trust says suspending Enniskillen emergency surgery improved patient outcomes BBC
